arxiv-1612-04531.creator: Xiaohu Ge, Song Tu, Guoqiang Mao, Vincent K. N. Lau, Linghui Pan, School of Electronic Information and Communications Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan 430074, Hubei, P. R. China. Email: {xhge, songtu, lhpan}@mail.hust.edu.cn School of Computing and Communications The University o
arxiv-1612-04531.description: Abstract The wireless backhaul network provides an attractive solution for the urban deployment of fifth generation (5G) wireless networks that enables future ultra dense small cell networks to meet the ever-increasing user demands. Optimal deployment and management of 5G wireless backhaul networks is an interesting and challenging issue.

arxiv-1907-10526.title: A Convolutional Forward and Back-Projection Model for Fan-Beam Geometry
arxiv-1907-10526.creator: Kai Zhang, Alireza Entezari
arxiv-1907-10526.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Kai Zhang, Alireza Entezari. Iterative methods for tomographic image reconstruction have great potential for enabling high quality imaging from low-dose projection data. The computational burden of iterative reconstruction algorithms, however, has been an impediment in their adoption in practical CT reconstruction problems. We present an approach for highly efficient and accurate computation of forward model for image reconstruction in fan-beam geometry in X-ray CT.

arxiv-2104-09016.title: Testing the effect of resolution on gravitational fragmentation with Lagrangian hydrodynamic schemes 2020 Testing the effect of resolution on gravitational fragmentation with Lagrangian hydrodynamic schemes – References
arxiv-2104-09016.creator: Yasuyoshi Yamamoto, Takashi Okamoto, Takayuki R. Saitoh
arxiv-2104-09016.description: Abstract To study the resolution required for simulating gravitational fragmentation with newly developed Lagrangian hydrodynamic schemes, Meshless Finite Volume method (MFV) and Meshless Finite Mass method (MFM), we have performed a number of simulations of the Jeans test and compared the results with both the expected analytic solution and results from the more standard Lagrangian approach: Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH).

arxiv-2110-10448.title: Gravitational Waves from GRB Core Spindown
arxiv-2110-10448.creator: I. Contopoulos, A. Strantzalis, D. Papadopoulos, D. Kazanas
arxiv-2110-10448.description: Abstract We investigate long Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRB) which manifest a sharp linear rise followed by an exponential decay in their γ \gamma -ray prompt emission observed with the BAT instrument on board the Swift satellite. We offer a simple electrodynamic model that may account for these particular characteristics.

arxiv-2111-00264.title: A Quasi-Newton method for physically-admissible simulation of Poiseuille flow under fracture propagation.
arxiv-2111-00264.creator: Guotong Ren, Rami M. Younis
arxiv-2111-00264.description: Abstract Coupled hydro-mechanical processes are of great importance to numerous engineering systems, e.g., hydraulic fracturing, geothermal energy, and carbon sequestration. Fluid flow in fractures is modeled after a Poiseuille law that relates the conductivity to the aperture by a cubic relation. Newton’s method is commonly employed to solve the resulting discrete, nonlinear algebraic systems.

arxiv-2201-03197.title: Perspective: Ultrafast Imaging of Molecular Dynamics Using Ultrafast Low-Frequency Lasers, X-ray Free Electron Laser and Electron Pulses
arxiv-2201-03197.creator: Ming Zhang, Zhengning Guo, Xiaoyu Mi, Zheng Li, Yunquan Liu
arxiv-2201-03197.description: Abstract Abstract The requirement of high space-time resolution and brightness is a great challenge for imaging atomic motion and making molecular movies. Important breakthroughs in ultrabright tabletop laser, x-ray and electron sources have enabled the direct imaging of evolving molecular structures in chemical processes.

arxiv-2206-13652.title: Reducing Polarization on Abortion, Guns and Immigration: An Experimental Study Thanks: The study was funded by Cornell University (Belot’s research funds). The authors thank Pilar Cardinale and Sarahi Osuna for excellent research support, and Nathan Maddox for very useful comments. We also thank the
arxiv-2206-13652.creator: Michèle Belot, Guglielmo Briscese
arxiv-2206-13652.description: Abstract We study individuals’ willingness to engage with others who hold opposite views on polarizing policies. A representative sample of 2,507 Americans are given the opportunity to listen to recordings of fellow countrymen and women expressing their views on immigration, abortion laws and gun ownership laws.

arxiv-2307-16246.title: DRL4Route: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Pick-up and Delivery Route Prediction Conference: Proceedings of the 29th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 6–10, 2023; Long Beach, CA, USA Proceedings of the 29th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery a
arxiv-2307-16246.creator: Xiaowei Mao †, Haomin Wen †, Hengrui Zhang, Huaiyu Wan, Lixia Wu, Jianbin Zheng, Haoyuan Hu, Youfang Lin
arxiv-2307-16246.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Xiaowei Mao †, Haomin Wen †, Hengrui Zhang, Huaiyu Wan, Lixia Wu, Jianbin Zheng, Haoyuan Hu, Youfang Lin. Pick-up and Delivery Route Prediction (PDRP), which aims to estimate the future service route of a worker given his current task pool, has received rising attention in recent years. Deep neural networks based on supervised learning have emerged as the dominant model for the task because of their powerful ability to capture workers’ behavior patterns from massive historical data.

arxiv-2401-06372.title: Spectral fit residuals as an indicator to increase model complexity
arxiv-2401-06372.creator: Anshuman Acharya, Vinay L. Kashyap
arxiv-2401-06372.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Anshuman Acharya, Vinay L. Kashyap. Spectral fitting of X-ray data usually involves minimizing statistics like the chi-square and the Cash statistic. Here we discuss their limitations and introduce two measures based on the cumulative sum (CuSum) of model residuals to evaluate whether model complexity could be increased: the percentage of bins exceeding a nominal threshold in a CuSum array (pct CuSum ), and the excess area under the CuSum compared to the nominal (p area {}_{\textit{area}} ).

arxiv-2406-01932.title: Detecting Endangered Marine Species in Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Imagery Using Point Annotations and Few-Shot Learning
arxiv-2406-01932.creator: Heather Doig, Oscar Pizarro, Jacquomo Monk, Stefan Williams
arxiv-2406-01932.description: Abstract One use of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) is the monitoring of habitats associated with threatened, endangered and protected marine species, such as the handfish of Tasmania, Australia. Seafloor imagery collected by AUVs can be used to identify individuals within their broader habitat context, but the sheer volume of imagery collected can overwhelm efforts to locate rare or cryptic individuals.

arxiv-2411-09749.title: RenderBender: A Survey on Adversarial Attacks Using Differentiable Rendering
arxiv-2411-09749.creator: Matthew Hull, Haoran Wang, Matthew Lau, Alec Helbling, Mansi Phute, Chao Zhang, Zsolt Kira, Willian Lunardi, Martin Andreoni, Wenke Lee, Polo Chau
arxiv-2411-09749.description: Abstract Differentiable rendering techniques like Gaussian Splatting and Neural Radiance Fields have become powerful tools for generating high-fidelity models of 3D objects and scenes. Their ability to produce both physically plausible and differentiable models of scenes are key ingredient needed to produce physically plausible adversarial attacks on DNNs.

arxiv-2506-10478.title: On the 4 4 -clique cover number of graphs
arxiv-2506-10478.creator: Yihan Chen, Jialin He, Tianying Xie
arxiv-2506-10478.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yihan Chen, Jialin He, Tianying Xie. In 1966, Erdős, Goodman, and Pósa proved that ⌊ n 2 / 4 ⌋ \lfloor n^{2}/4\rfloor cliques are sufficient to cover all edges in any n n -vertex graph, with tightness achieved by the balanced complete bipartite graph.

arxiv-2510-11722.title: eye2vec: Learning Distributed Representations of Eye Movement for Program Comprehension Analysis Conference: 2025 Symposium on Eye Tracking Research and Applications; May 26–29, 2025; Tokyo, Japan 2025 Symposium on Eye Tracking Research and Applications (ETRA ’25), May 26–29, 2025, Tokyo, Japan DOI:
arxiv-2510-11722.creator: Haruhiko Yoshioka, Kazumasa Shimari, Hidetake Uwano, Kenichi Matsumoto
arxiv-2510-11722.description: Abstract . This paper presents eye2vec , an infrastructure for analyzing software developers’ eye movements while reading source code. In common eye-tracking studies in program comprehension, researchers must preselect analysis targets such as control flow or syntactic elements, and then develop analysis methods to extract appropriate metrics from the fixation for source code.

gregory-of-nyssa-on-not-three-gods-npnf2.title: On 'Not Three Gods'
gregory-of-nyssa-on-not-three-gods-npnf2.creator: Gregory of Nyssa
gregory-of-nyssa-on-not-three-gods-npnf2.description: On 'Not Three Gods' — Gregory of Nyssa. From the Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Series 2 edition (1892). A principal work of the early church, among the foundational texts of Christian antiquity.

plos-pone-0002395.title: Continued Neurogenesis in Adult Drosophila as a Mechanism for Recruiting Environmental Cue-Dependent Variants
plos-pone-0002395.creator: Selim Ben Rokia-Mille, Sylvette Tinette, Gilbert Engler et al.
plos-pone-0002395.description: PLOS ONE research article. The skills used by winged insects to explore their environment are strongly dependent upon the integration of neurosensory information comprising visual, acoustic and olfactory signals. The neuronal architecture of the wing contains a vast array of different sensors which might c

pmc-11623829.title: Emerging trends and hotspots in lung cancer-prediction models research
pmc-11623829.creator: Qiong Ma, Hua Jiang, Shiyan Tan, Fengming You, Chuan Zheng, Qian Wang, Yifeng Ren
pmc-11623829.description: Objective:In recent years, lung cancer-prediction models have become popular. However, few bibliometric analyses have been performed in this field.Methods:This study aimed to reveal the scientific output and trends in lung cancer-prediction models from a global perspective. In this study, publications were retrieved and extracted from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) database. CiteSpace 6.1.R3 and VOSviewer 1.6.

pmc-11657369.title: Exosome-delivered NR2F1-AS1 and NR2F1 drive phenotypic transition from dormancy to proliferation in treatment-resistant prostate cancer via stabilizing hormonal receptors
pmc-11657369.creator: Wenbin Chen, Yiyou Mao, YiYuan Zhan, Wenfeng Li, Jun Wu, Xiangming Mao, Bin Xu, Fangpeng Shu
pmc-11657369.description: Cancer cells acquire the ability to reprogram their phenotype in response to targeted therapies, yet the transition from dormancy to proliferation in drug-resistant cancers remains poorly understood. In prostate cancer, we utilized high-plasticity mouse models and enzalutamide-resistant (ENZ-R) cellular models to elucidate NR2F1 as a key factor in lineage transition and ENZ resistance.

pmc-12525429.title: Perioperative Repercussions of Cannabis Use—Implications for GI Endoscopy Sedation
pmc-12525429.creator: Basavana Goudra, Michael Green, Eleni Laou, Eleana Garini, Giolanda Varvarousi
pmc-12525429.description: The legalization of cannabis in multiple U.S. states and several other countries, along with its increasing social acceptance across diverse demographic and socioeconomic groups, has led to a growing number of patients presenting for interventional procedures with a history of cannabis use.

pmc-12660513.title: Semaglutide in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis: A Narrative Review
pmc-12660513.creator: George S Zacharia, Sudharsan R Gongati, Aayush Kharel, Anu Jacob
pmc-12660513.description: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), an incretin hormone, plays a crucial role in glucose homeostasis by stimulating insulin secretion, suppressing glucagon release, and delaying gastric emptying. Its therapeutic potential was long realized, leading to the development of the first GLP-1 receptor agonist, exenatide, followed by liraglutide, dulaglutide, semaglutide, and tirzepatide. Semaglutide is available as a weekly subcutaneous injection with high bioavailability.

pmc-12689888.title: A test of the mediating effects of social interaction, physical fitness, and alleviation of negative emotions in the influence of physical exercise on residents' subjective wellbeing—empirical analysis based on CGSS 2023
pmc-12689888.creator: Shutong Zhao, Haiyan Huang
pmc-12689888.description: IntroductionParticipation in physical exercise (PE) can effectively enhance residents' subjective wellbeing; however, additional research is warranted to elucidate the mechanisms by which exercise participation influences population wellbeing. This study aims to investigate the impact of physical exercise on residents' subjective wellbeing and explore its mediating mechanisms, offering deeper insights into the psychological effects of exercise.

pmc-12690402.title: The Use of Parabulbar and Sub‐Tenon Injections to Correct Isolated Resistant Diplopia in Patients With Generalized Myasthenia Gravis: A Long Road to Clinically Meaningful Success
pmc-12690402.creator: M. Marchuk, V. Sanin, V. Mamilov, M. Zinchenko
pmc-12690402.description: Parabulbar betamethasone provided rapid and durable relief of isolated, treatment‐resistant diplopia in seronegative myasthenia gravis after multiple systemic therapy failures, suggesting that targeted periocular corticosteroid delivery may be a steroid‐sparing option for carefully selected patients when standard treatments are ineffective and close ophthalmic monitoring is available.

pmc-13054980.title: A novel hairless highly immunodeficient mice model optimized for in vivo imaging
pmc-13054980.creator: Kouki Matsuda, Ryusho Kariya, Sawako Fujikawa, Kenji Maeda, Seiji Okada
pmc-13054980.description: BackgroundIn vivo imaging is one of the analytical technologies that has been rapidly growing in demand in recent years to non-invasively observe the behavior of molecules such as genes and proteins in vivo and perform quantitative and qualitative analysis. Since the hair blocks and absorbs the fluorescence, Nude and Hairless mice have been used for in vivo imaging.

pmc-13081634.title: Hybrid metabolic engineering enables xylose-driven co-production of polyhydroxybutyrate and violacein in Escherichia coli
pmc-13081634.creator: Khoi Nhat Pham, Eun Yeol Lee
pmc-13081634.description: BackgroundWithin lignocellulosic biomass, xylose is the second most abundant sugar after glucose. As a renewable and sustainable substrate, it is gaining attention as a feedstock for microbial bioprocesses. In this study, we demonstrated the co-production of polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) and violacein from xylose.

pmc-13427353.title: Immune Polarization in Coexisting Rheumatoid Arthritis and Asthma: Insights into Th2 Dominance and Unresolved Confounding
pmc-13427353.creator: Nedim Kaban

pmc-13533038.title: Analgesic Prescribing Trends of Opioids, Nonsteroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs, and Paracetamol in Taiwan (2001‐2020): Age-Period-Cohort Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13533038.creator: Chun-Ji Lin, Chia-Shuan Chang, Chih-Yi Wu, Jiun-Yi Wang, I-Ching Lin, Hung-Yi Chiou, Amaryllis Mavragani, Travis Sanchez
pmc-13533038.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundDespite ongoing global changes in analgesic prescribing practices, long-term trends accounting for age, period, and cohort effects remain poorly understood in Asian populations, where opioid and nonopioid prescribing trajectories differ from those observed in Western nations.ObjectiveThis study aimed to examine the long-term prescribing trends of opioids, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), and paracetamol in Taiwan by age, calendar period, and birth cohort using an age-period-cohort (APC) framework.MethodsWe conducted a population-based repeated cross-sectional study using Taiwan National Health Insurance claims data (2001‐2020).

pmc-13613103.title: The Interplay of PD-L1, Kynurenine Pathway, and Vitamin D Shapes an Immunosuppressive Microenvironment in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
pmc-13613103.creator: Amit Choudhary, Ramya Ramesh, Rakhee Kar, Prakash Babu Narasimhan, Prasanth Ganesan, Biswajit Dubashi, Rajesh NG, Soundravally R, Smita Kayal
pmc-13613103.description: Background:Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a genetically heterogeneous malignancy. However, the immune microenvironment-including immune checkpoint pathways and metabolic regulators also plays a pivotal role in disease progression.Aims:To investigate the immune-metabolic landscape of newly diagnosed AML patients, focusing on the PDL1-PD1 and IDO-Kynurenine-AhR pathways, and their association with vitamin D levels.Setting:A prospective, observational study conducted at a tertiary care academic hospital.

pmc-13650339.title: Changes in cardiovascular risk factors in patients with inflammatory arthritis following screening consultations—a Danish register-based cohort study
pmc-13650339.creator: Julie Katrine Karstensen, Sonja Wehberg, Anja Bachmann, Kim Hørslev-Petersen, Jens Søndergaard, Anette Hvenegaard Kjeldgaard, Jette Primdahl
pmc-13650339.description: ObjectivesPatients with chronic inflammatory arthritis (IA) (rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and axial spondyloarthritis) have an increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD). Although the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) recommends systematic cardiovascular risk (CVR) management in these patients, knowledge about whether CVR management programmes significantly reduce risk factors and, thus, overall CVR in patients with IA remains limited.
